about.title: About
about.p1Html: I'm Aron Jake Radam (also known online as ), a Game Developer focusing on gameplay systems, Unity tooling, and technical game design. I got my start in game playtesting and QA at GridLock-Games Studio, testing builds and reporting bugs while collaborating with developers and designers on gameplay feel, balance, and release readiness.
about.haruOriginHtml: Haru means "spring" in Japanese, -chan is a casual Japanese suffix, and Z64 comes from the Nintendo 64 games The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask (my very first Zelda game) and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. It started as a gaming username, and I've kept using it on GitHub and my socials.
about.p2Html: After that, I worked as the sole full-stack engineer at PicStar Software OPC in Las Piñas, Philippines, where I architected PicStar with Flutter and Supabase and shipped it to the Google Play Store. That work sharpened my discipline in live backends, performance, and shipping production software end to end.
about.p3Html: Today, I build open-source Unity editor tools and runtime systems to speed up designer and QA workflows while teaching as a College Instructor under the BS EMC (Game Development) program at the University of Caloocan City. I guide sophomore through senior students across game design theory, prototyping, OOP, game math, AI, networking, and production pipelines.
about.p4Html: I also keep studying game design theory and use AI coding tools in my daily workflow to prototype and debug faster. I'm open to game studio roles, freelance projects, and collaborations.

0.b0: Teach game design theory, rapid prototyping, and production pipelines to sophomore through senior students, guiding game projects from initial mechanics to playable builds.
0.b1: Lead lectures and lab sessions on game programming, systems architecture, networking, and production workflows, helping students turn design docs into working prototypes.
0.b2: Cover core scripting and engine fundamentals including OOP, math in games, physics, collision detection, game AI, networking, and code optimization.
0.b3: Mentor student teams through lab reviews, debugging sessions, and playtest critiques grounded in current game studio practices.

1.b0: Owned the technical direction and day-to-day engineering of a social media mobile application as the sole engineer, from architecture through deployment.
1.b1: Built the cross-platform mobile app in Flutter with a modular codebase and consistent UI/UX.
1.b2: Designed and maintained the Supabase PostgreSQL backend, tuning queries, data egress, and real-time feeds.
1.b3: Implemented core PicStar features including the Top and Board feeds, Shineouts for promoting posts and shots from Board to Top, Top rankings, and city-based content filtering.
1.b4: Engineered and deployed PicStar to the Google Play Store on October 11, 2026, releasing the Flutter app and Supabase backend into production.

2.b0: Partnered with game developers and designers to test gameplay builds, catch edge-case regressions, and flag usability issues before release.
2.b1: Logged, reproduced, and tracked bugs in Trello with clear reproduction steps to keep engineering and design fixes moving smoothly.
2.b2: Supported the full game release cycle through structured regression testing and build verification.

3.b0: Playtested in-development game builds to uncover gameplay bugs, physics glitches, and mechanics exploits.
3.b1: Delivered structured written and verbal feedback on core gameplay loops, pacing, balance, and game feel.
3.b2: Collaborated directly with developers to document reproduction steps clearly and verify fixes across patches.

0.degree: BS in Entertainment and Multimedia Computing
0.b0: Developed Trash Frenzy for our capstone project, an educational game for Grade 5 students and above that raises water pollution awareness in the Philippines and teaches proper waste disposal through storytelling and gameplay.
0.b1: Served as Project Manager, Game Designer, Game Programmer, and Game QA in a four-member team, coordinating project milestones, designing gameplay mechanics and narrative flow, implementing core systems, and testing builds for quality assurance.
0.b2: Completed coursework in Introduction to Game Design and Development, Advanced Game Design, Game Programming 1–3, Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Games, Applied Mathematics for Games, Game Networking, and Game Production.
